{{short description|Italian physicist}}
[[Image:Zavattini.jpg|frame|Portrait of Emilio Zavattini.]]

'''Emilio Zavattini''' (March 14, 1927 – January 9, 2007) was an Italian [[Particle physics|particle physicist.]]<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-540-73518-2|title=Axions: Theory, Cosmology, and Experimental Searches|date=2008|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|isbn=978-3-540-73517-5|editor-last=Kuster|editor-first=Markus|series=Lecture Notes in Physics|volume=741|location=Berlin, Heidelberg|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-73518-2|quote=Front matter|editor-last2=Raffelt|editor-first2=Georg|editor-last3=Beltrán|editor-first3=Berta }}</ref>

==Biography==
He was born in [[Rimini, Italy|Rimini]], [[Italy]] and enrolled in the [[University of Rome La Sapienza]] as a physics student in 1950 and earned his [[doctorate]] in 1954.

Zavattini joined [[CERN]] in 1955 and remained a staff member until he retired in 1992.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Emilio Zavattini 65|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1732027|journal=CERN Courier|volume=32|issue=4|pages=19}}</ref> Early in this period he made a short post-doctoral visit to [[Nevis Laboratories|Nevis Laboratory]] at [[Columbia University]] where he worked with [[Leon M. Lederman|Leon Lederman]]. After retirement, he held a position as a professor at the [[University of Trieste]] from 1988–1999.<ref>{{Cite web|title=14 marzo 1927 - Nasce a Rimini Emilio "Mimmo" Zavattini, il "fisico del vuoto" del CERN|url=https://www.chiamamicitta.it/14-marzo-1927-nasce-rimini-emilio-mimmo-zavattini-fisico-del-vuoto-del-cern/|date=2020-03-13|website=Chiamamicitta|language=it-IT|access-date=2020-05-14|archive-date=2021-03-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210317173540/https://www.chiamamicitta.it/14-marzo-1927-nasce-rimini-emilio-mimmo-zavattini-fisico-del-vuoto-del-cern/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Zavattini is known for the [[Muon g-2#Muon g − 2 at CERN|muon g-2]] experiment and the [[PVLAS|PVLAS experiment]] at the INFN [[Laboratori Nazionali di Legnaro|Laboratory in Legnaro]] (Padua, Italy). He made contributions within the fields of [[strong interaction|strong]], [[weak interaction|weak]] and [[electromagnetic interaction]]s—especially using [[muon]]s—both at [[CERN]] and at other European and U.S. laboratories. In later years his studies focused on a better understanding of the [[Vacuum state|structure of vacuum]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emilio Zavattini - 1927-2007|url=https://cds.cern.ch/journal/CERNBulletin/2007/05/News%20Articles/1010520?ln=en|website=CERN Document Server|access-date=2020-05-14}}</ref>

He was a member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]].

Zavattini died at the age of 79 of a [[heart attack]].
